about.title: About Calorie Calculator
about.description: The Calorie Calculator estimates your daily caloric needs based on age, gender, weight, height, and activity level. It calculates your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) to help you maintain, lose, or gain weight effectively. Understanding your caloric needs is essential for achieving fitness goals, whether you're trying to lose weight, build muscle, or maintain your current weight. The calculator provides personalized recommendations based on scientifically proven formulas.

faq.q: What's the difference between BMR and TDEE in calorie calculation?
faq.a: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the calories your body burns at rest for basic functions like breathing and circulation. TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) includes BMR plus calories burned through daily activities and exercise. Our calorie calculator provides both values for comprehensive planning.

faq.q: How accurate are calorie calculator estimates?
faq.a: Calorie calculators provide estimates based on population averages using proven formulas like Mifflin-St Jeor. Individual metabolism can vary by 10-15%, so use our calculator results as a starting point and adjust based on your actual progress and energy levels.

faq.q: Should I eat exactly the calculated daily calories?
faq.a: Use our calorie calculation as a baseline. Monitor your weight, energy levels, and progress, then adjust intake up or down by 100-200 calories as needed to reach your specific goals. The calculator provides a scientifically-based starting point.

faq.q: How often should I recalculate my daily calorie needs?
faq.a: Recalculate your calorie needs every 10-15 pounds of weight change, or every 2-3 months if your activity level changes significantly. Our calculator accounts for these changes to maintain accuracy.

faq.q: What activity level should I choose in the calorie calculator?
faq.a: Be honest about your activity level: Sedentary (desk job, no exercise), Lightly Active (light exercise 1-3 days/week), Moderately Active (moderate exercise 3-5 days/week), Very Active (hard exercise 6-7 days/week), or Extremely Active (very hard exercise, physical job).

faq.q: Can I use this calorie calculator for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, our calorie calculator is excellent for weight loss planning. It calculates your maintenance calories, then you can create a deficit of 500-1000 calories per day for safe weight loss of 1-2 pounds per week. Always consult healthcare providers for personalized advice.
